blank:0.en: Inside the cabin, Old Helm spread a wide map across the table. Most of it was empty — a great *blank* where unknown islands should have been. 'Every word we find fills one part of it,' he said, tapping the pale space with one finger. I leaned in close, already wanting to fill every gap.

reading:0.en: Bell sat cross-legged on a crate near the lantern, deep in her evening *reading*. The pages were covered in tiny drawings of island shapes and star angles. 'This is how I learn the sky,' she told me, not looking up. The warm light made the whole cabin feel like a quiet secret.

reading:0.hook: Then she turned to a page with no drawings — only a single unknown word.

list:0.en: Old Helm handed me a folded paper on my first morning aboard. It was a *list* of every word the troupe had ever collected, each one followed by the name of the island it had unlocked. I counted thirty-seven entries. The thirty-eighth line was blank, and that felt like an invitation.

select:0.line: 'You must *select* with care; that word becomes our next sky.'

need:0.en: 'Before we leave, there is one thing we *need*,' Old Helm said, setting down his cup. He pointed to the small brass lock on the ship's front door. The key had been missing since before I joined. Bell produced it from her coat pocket with a quiet grin, and the whole cabin seemed to breathe out.

passage:1.en: Old Helm spread the old map across a barrel at the edge of the dock. A narrow *passage* between two crumbling stone towers marked the only way to the upper islands. Bell traced it with one finger, her eyes wide. 'That gap looks barely wide enough for our ship,' she said softly.

base:1.en: The troupe gathered at the *base* of a great stone pillar rising from the dock square. Worn carvings covered its surface all the way up. Old Helm pressed his palm flat against the cold rock and smiled. 'Every journey needs a solid place to begin,' he said, patting the stone.

answer:1.en: A local dock-hand pointed at the symbol on Old Helm's map and shook his head slowly. Old Helm asked him twice what it meant. The man opened his mouth, paused, then gave a short *answer* in a language none of us knew — and walked away before we could ask anything more.

letter:1.en: On the morning we set sail, Old Helm spread a worn map across the deck. At its corner sat a single folded paper. 'Each *letter* on this map,' he said softly, 'is a door.' I traced the strange shapes with my finger and felt the sky above us shift.

single:1.en: We passed through a market crowd so thick I could barely breathe. Then, at the far edge, a *single* lantern hung above a narrow door. No sign. No sound. Old Helm stopped and stared at it for a long moment. Bell touched my shoulder gently and whispered, 'That one matters.'
single:1.cnHint: 嘈杂市集的边缘，一盏____的灯笼悬挂在一扇无名小门上方。

line:1.line: 'Follow this *line* of words and it will take you to the first island,' said Old Helm.

become:1.hook: Old Helm said nothing — he simply handed me the compass.
become:1.line: 'You will *become* a fine word-keeper,' Old Helm said, still smiling.

centre:1.en: The troupe gathered at the *centre* of the harbour square, where an old stone pillar rose from the cobblestones. Maps, scraps of paper, and small flags covered it on all sides. Travellers had left pieces of their journeys here. Old Helm pressed his palm flat against the stone and closed his eyes.
centre:1.cnHint: 剧团聚集在港口广场____的石柱旁，上面贴满了旅人留下的地图碎片。

centre:1.line: 'Every great journey,' said Old Helm, 'starts from a *centre* that holds still.'

comprehension:0.line: '*Comprehension* is the key that opens every door on the chart.'

decide:0.cnHint: 旅团成员聚在一起____首先拜访哪座浮岛，最终把选择权交给了我。

item:1.hook: The humming grew louder the higher I lifted it.
item:1.line: 'Never leave without this *item* — it reads the wind.'

select:1.en: Silverfang stood at the centre of the dock, arms folded, watching the crew move around him. He did not pick just anyone for the crossing — he would *select* only those who could tie three kinds of knot without looking. I practised all night to earn my place beside him.
select:1.cnHint: 竞争船长不随便招募船员，他会仔细____真正有本领的人。
select:1.hook: He looked at my hands, then gave one slow nod.
select:1.line: 'I *select* my crew the way a star selects its sky — carefully.'

need:1.en: The sky-boat groaned as the last rope was cast off. Old Helm turned to me with a steady look. 'You *need* to keep your eyes on the horizon at all times,' he said. 'The islands move with the wind, and a blink is enough to lose one.' I gripped the rail and did not blink.
need:1.cnHint: 老舵手郑重告诉我，出发前____做好一件非常重要的事。
need:1.hook: Ahead, the first island was already drifting left.
need:1.line: 'You *need* to trust the stars more than your feet right now.'

letter:2.en: Bell found the old chest wedged under the navigation deck. Inside lay a single folded paper — a *letter* written in careful script, addressed to no one by name, yet somehow meant for whoever opened it. 'Every word here is a map,' she said, eyes wide.
letter:2.cnHint: 小铃在航行甲板下发现了一个旧箱子，里面有一封____，似乎是专为打开它的人写的。
letter:2.hook: The signature at the bottom had been torn away.
letter:2.line: 'This *letter* knows exactly where we need to go,' Bell said softly.

sheet:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a large *sheet* of pale paper across the deck table. On it, faint dotted lines traced the shapes of islands none of us had ever seen. The wind lifted one corner, and for a moment the whole map seemed to breathe like something alive.
sheet:2.cnHint: 老舵长在甲板桌上展开一张____，上面画着从未见过的岛屿轮廓。
sheet:2.hook: One island at the edge had no name — only a question mark.
sheet:2.line: 'Every *sheet* we find adds another piece to the sky,' Old Helm said.

corresponding:2.en: Bell held the star chart up to the dawn light. Each bright point had a *corresponding* symbol etched below it, matching a word carved into our ship's mast. 'The sky and the ship are talking to each other,' she whispered, tracing the pattern with one careful finger.
corresponding:2.cnHint: 小铃发现星图上的每个亮点都有一个____符号，与船桅上刻的文字相互对应。
corresponding:2.hook: One symbol on the mast had never been lit — until now.
corresponding:2.line: 'Find the *corresponding* mark on deck, and the door will open,' Bell said.

choose:2.en: Three paths of cloud stretched ahead of the ship, each leading to a different island on the horizon. Old Helm looked at us in turn. 'We can only sail one way before the wind shifts,' he said. 'So *choose* well.' The whole troupe fell quiet, thinking hard.
choose:2.cnHint: 前方出现三条云路，老舵长要求大家____一条航线，因为风向即将改变。
choose:2.hook: Silverfang was already pointing, a strange smile on his face.
choose:2.line: '*Choose* the middle cloud — I have sailed there before,' Old Helm said.

single:2.en: We searched the cave wall for hours, finding nothing. Then Bell pressed her palm flat against the stone and felt it — one thin groove, running top to bottom. A *single* carved line, no wider than a finger, glowing faintly gold. The whole cave seemed to hold its breath.
single:2.cnHint: 在洞穴中搜寻许久后，小铃终于感觉到墙上有一道____刻痕，散发着微弱的金光。
single:2.hook: Touching it made the floor beneath us begin to shift.
single:2.line: 'Not one *single* mark on this wall was made by accident,' Bell said.

line:2.en: Silverfang leaned over the railing and pointed down. Far below the ship, a thin ribbon of golden light crossed the clouds — a perfect *line* dividing the dark sky from the bright. 'That,' he said quietly, 'is the border of the next island's reach. We cross it at dawn.'
line:2.cnHint: 竞争船长指着船下方一道金色的____，说那是下一座岛屿领域的边界。
line:2.hook: No ship in the troupe's memory had ever crossed it before dawn.
line:2.line: 'Follow that *line* of light, and the island will rise to meet you,' Silverfang said.

become:2.en: Old Helm handed me a worn compass and said nothing for a long moment. 'Every navigator in this troupe started exactly where you are standing,' he said at last. 'The sky does not care where you were born. It only cares what you *become*.' I held the compass tighter.
become:2.cnHint: 老舵长递给我一枚旧罗盘，告诉我天空只在乎你____什么，而非你来自哪里。
become:2.hook: The compass needle swung — and pointed straight at me.
become:2.line: 'Sail long enough, and you will *become* someone the stars remember,' Old Helm said.

centre:2.en: The fog parted slowly, and there it was — a small, perfectly round island floating at the exact *centre* of four converging wind streams. Every gust curved toward it as if bowing. Bell marked it on the chart with a red dot and circled it twice. 'That is where we land,' she said.
centre:2.cnHint: 迷雾散开后，众人看到一座圆形小岛悬浮在四股气流的____，小铃立刻在地图上标记了它。
centre:2.hook: Something on that island was already sending light toward our ship.
centre:2.line: 'Whatever we are looking for, it is at the *centre* of that island,' Bell said.

bank:2.en: Bell led us down a rope ladder to a narrow *bank* of white sand curving along the edge of the island. She knelt and pressed her palm flat against the ground. 'Words sleep here,' she said softly. Beneath the sand, faint letters glowed like buried stars.
bank:2.cnHint: 小铃带领大家来到岛边的____，发现沙下藏着发光的文字。
bank:2.hook: The letters rearranged themselves into a shape none of us recognised.
bank:2.line: 'Stay close to the *bank* — the sand only glows where the words are hidden.'

statement:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a strip of bark and read aloud the *statement* carved into it: 'Only those who carry wonder may pass.' The words hung in the air like smoke. We looked at each other. Nobody spoke. The gate ahead trembled, waiting.
statement:2.cnHint: 老舵读出刻在树皮上的一段____，大门随之颤动起来。
statement:2.hook: Something behind the gate exhaled a long, slow breath.
statement:2.line: 'Read the *statement* again — I want every word to land before we move.'

identify:2.en: The map fragment shimmered with dozens of tiny symbols, and Bell asked me to *identify* the one that matched the mark on my sleeve. My heart jumped. I had worn that sleeve patch since childhood without ever knowing its meaning. I pressed my finger to the symbol, and it lit up gold.
identify:2.cnHint: 小铃让我____袖子上的符号，没想到那个标记竟与地图上的一个图案完全吻合。
identify:2.hook: A door-shaped outline cracked open in the empty sky above us.
identify:2.line: 'Can you *identify* the symbol? Your mark may be the key we need.'

comprehension:2.en: Old Helm spread the glowing chart across a flat stone and tested my *comprehension* of the star-paths marked on it. I traced each line slowly. He nodded, then added a new line I had never seen before. 'The island moves,' he said. 'Your reading must move with it.'
comprehension:2.cnHint: 老舵用星图测试我的____，并告诉我那座岛屿是会移动的。
comprehension:2.hook: The new line on the chart pulsed once, then pointed somewhere unexpected.
comprehension:2.line: 'Good — your *comprehension* of the star-paths will keep us from drifting.'

require:2.en: The bridge of crystal between two islands looked beautiful, but a carved sign warned that it would *require* a spoken word to hold our weight. Bell whispered the word 'trust' without hesitation. The bridge rang like a bell and turned solid beneath our feet.
require:2.cnHint: 水晶桥的告示说过桥____说出一个词语，小铃毫不犹豫地开口了。
require:2.hook: Halfway across, I felt the bridge begin to hum a second warning.
require:2.line: 'The bridge will *require* a true word — choose the one you believe.'

least:2.en: We counted our remaining map fragments. Old Helm sighed. 'We have the *least* we have ever carried.' But Bell pointed out that every great journey had begun with almost nothing. She held up the single glowing piece, and it cast light far enough to show the next island waiting on the horizon.
least:2.cnHint: 碎片所剩____，但小铃举起仅剩的一块，它的光芒足以照见远处的下一座岛屿。
least:2.hook: That fragment pulsed twice — as if it already knew where we were going.
least:2.line: 'At *least* one fragment still glows — and that is enough to sail by.'

following:2.en: Bell posted a short list on the mast before we set off. It read: 'The *following* rules keep the troupe safe — speak every new word aloud, trust the wind, and never sail past a glowing stone.' Old Helm smiled when he saw it. He added one more rule at the bottom.
following:2.cnHint: 出发前，小铃把____几条规定贴在桅杆上，老舵看完后又悄悄补充了一条。
following:2.hook: Old Helm's added rule was written in a language none of us could read.
following:2.line: 'The *following* three rules are not suggestions — they are how we survive.'

decide:2.en: Two cloud-roads stretched before us, one gold and one silver. Old Helm turned to me and said I must *decide* which path the troupe would take. My mouth went dry. Bell leaned close and whispered, 'The words you have collected so far — let them guide you.' I closed my eyes and chose.
decide:2.cnHint: 面对两条云路，老舵让我来____走哪一条，小铃悄悄提示我用已收集的词语来引导判断。
decide:2.hook: The moment my foot touched the chosen path, both roads vanished behind us.
decide:2.line: 'You must *decide* now — the cloud-roads will not wait past sunrise.'

blank:2.en: Bell spread the old map across the deck and pointed to a wide *blank* near the centre. 'That space means no one has been there yet,' she said softly. Old Helm smiled and placed a newly found word-fragment right over it. The gap shimmered, and a faint island outline began to appear.
blank:2.cnHint: 小铃发现地图中央有一处____，贴上词语碎片后，岛屿的轮廓渐渐浮现。
blank:2.hook: The outline trembled, then split into two separate islands.
blank:2.line: 'Every *blank* on the map is a place waiting for us to find it.'

reading:2.en: I found a small folded note tucked inside the ship's lantern. The *reading* was short — just eight words — but Old Helm went very still when I handed it to him. He read it three times, lips moving, then looked up at a distant cloud with bright eyes.
reading:2.cnHint: 我在船灯里发现一张纸条，老舵手对这段____的反应让全船人屏息。
reading:2.hook: He whispered a name none of us had ever heard before.
reading:2.line: 'This *reading* changes where we sail next — pack your things tonight.'

list:2.en: Old Helm pinned a long *list* to the mast each morning — words collected, words still missing, islands ahead. Today the list was shorter than usual. Bell counted the remaining words quietly, then looked at me with a wide grin and held up three fingers.
list:2.cnHint: 老舵手每天把词语____钉在桅杆上，今天小铃数完后露出了神秘的笑容。
list:2.hook: Three words left, and the last one was said to be impossible to find.
list:2.line: 'Cross it off the *list* — we earned that word fair and square.'

item:2.en: Each word-fragment the troupe collected was stored in a glass jar as a glowing *item* no bigger than a coin. I held the newest one up to the starlight and it spun slowly, casting tiny maps across my palm. Bell said every item had its own small memory inside.
item:2.cnHint: 每个词语碎片都作为一件发光的____保存在玻璃罐里，据说每件都藏着记忆。
item:2.hook: The jar suddenly rattled, as if something inside wanted out.
item:2.line: 'Handle each *item* with care — a cracked one loses its island forever.'

select:2.en: Old Helm told me I could *select* one word-fragment from the jar to carry in my own pocket for the day. I looked at each glowing piece for a long time. When I finally chose, Bell laughed and said I had picked the very same one she would have taken.
select:2.cnHint: 老舵长让我从罐中____一枚词语碎片自己保管，小铃说我和她想到一块儿去了。
select:2.hook: The fragment grew warm the moment I stepped toward the bow.
select:2.line: 'You may *select* any one you like, but trust what your hand reaches for first.'

need:2.en: The ship began to slow above a bank of thick cloud. Bell checked the jar and frowned. 'We *need* one more word before the next island will show itself,' she said. Old Helm was already climbing the rigging, scanning the sky with calm, steady eyes.
need:2.cnHint: 船速减慢了，小铃说在下一座岛屿显现之前，我们____再找到一个词语碎片。
need:2.hook: High above, Old Helm suddenly pointed and shouted one clear word.
need:2.line: 'We *need* that fragment before the stars shift — move quickly.'

passage:2.en: We landed on a narrow island shaped like a bridge between two larger ones. Bell held up a rolled paper she had pulled from a stone post. 'This is a *passage* from the old map-keepers,' she said. The words on it glowed faintly, and a new path opened in the clouds ahead.
passage:2.cnHint: 小铃在石柱上找到一段古老的____，照亮了前方的云中小路。
passage:2.hook: The glowing words faded — but only after burning a new shape into the sky.
passage:2.line: 'This *passage* is older than any island we have visited.'

base:2.en: The crystal tower rose so high I had to lean back to see its top. Old Helm knelt and pressed one hand flat against the stone at its *base*, feeling the hum inside. 'This is where the word is hidden,' he said quietly. Above us, light began to move in slow circles.
base:2.cnHint: 老舵在高塔的____处感受到了振动，断定字词就藏在这里。
base:2.hook: The hum grew louder, and the ground beneath us began to lift.
base:2.line: 'Touch the *base* — you will feel what I mean.'

section:2.en: Bell spread the map across a flat rock and pointed to a small dark square. 'We have never visited this *section*,' she said. It sat between two islands we had already marked, easy to miss. Old Helm smiled and said it was exactly the kind of place that hid the best words.
section:2.cnHint: 小铃发现地图上有一个从未去过的____，那里可能藏着新的词语。
section:2.hook: The dark square suddenly flickered with a pale, warm light.
section:2.line: 'That *section* of the map has been blank since I joined this troupe.'

answer:2.en: I had been staring at the carved symbols on the cave wall for nearly an hour. Then Silverfang walked past, glanced up, and laughed softly. 'The *answer* is the shape of the island itself,' he said. I looked again — and he was right. The wall was a perfect outline of where we stood.
answer:2.cnHint: 银牙一眼看穿了石壁符号的____，原来那正是小岛本身的轮廓。
answer:2.hook: Outside the cave, the island shuddered, as if it had heard us.
answer:2.line: 'Sometimes the *answer* is the place you forgot to look at.'

study:2.en: Old Helm kept a small room at the back of the sky-ship filled with pressed leaves and star charts. He called it his *study*. That morning I found him there, eyes bright, holding a tiny glass bottle with a single word floating inside it like a caught firefly.
study:2.cnHint: 老舵在他的____里找到了一个装着词语的小玻璃瓶，像捕捉到的萤火虫。
study:2.hook: He handed me the bottle, and the word inside changed shape.
study:2.line: 'Come to my *study* — I want to show you what we found last night.'

mark:2.en: Bell drew a small circle on the inside of my wrist with a sky-blue pen. 'This *mark* means you belong to the troupe now,' she said with a warm smile. Old Helm nodded from across the deck. I looked down at it and felt, for the first time, that I was exactly where I was meant to be.
mark:2.cnHint: 小铃在我手腕上画了一个____，正式宣告我成为队伍的一员。
mark:2.hook: The mark warmed faintly when the next island came into view.
mark:2.line: 'Every member of this troupe carries the same *mark*.'

choice:2.en: Two cloud-bridges stretched away from the platform where we stood. One led toward a bright, warm glow. The other disappeared into soft silver mist. Old Helm folded his arms and looked at me. 'This *choice* is yours,' he said. 'You are the one who found the word that brought us here.'
choice:2.cnHint: 两条云桥通向不同方向，老舵把这次的____权交给了初来的我。
choice:2.hook: Both bridges began to hum at the same moment.
choice:2.line: 'It is your *choice* — we will follow wherever you go.'

part:2.en: Silverfang pulled a small brass gear from his coat pocket and set it on the table. 'This is the missing *part*,' he said. He pressed it into the center of the old device, and the whole machine woke with a soft click and a ring of rising light. The next island appeared on the map at once.
part:2.cnHint: 银牙找到了装置缺失的____，机器重新运转，新岛屿出现在地图上。
part:2.hook: The light ring spun faster, pointing like a finger toward the horizon.
part:2.line: 'Without this *part*, the machine could never show us the way.'

bank:1.en: We landed on the edge of a floating island where the ground dropped away like a river *bank*, soft soil crumbling into open sky. Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the earth. 'The word is here,' he said. Below us, clouds moved slowly, and somewhere beyond them a new island was waiting.
bank:1.cnHint: 老舵手在悬崖边缘发现了线索，脚下的土地像____一样向下延伸进云层。
bank:1.hook: One step too many and the sky would swallow you whole.
bank:1.line: 'Stand back from the *bank* — the edge is softer than it looks.'

statement:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a worn cloth map and read aloud the words stitched into it. Each word was a *statement* left by travellers long gone, a clear message that said: we were here, and the path continues. I copied the words into my own notebook, hands steady, heart racing.
statement:1.cnHint: 老舵手大声朗读地图上的文字，每个词都是前人留下的____。
statement:1.hook: The last stitched word pointed somewhere no map had ever shown.
statement:1.line: 'Every word on this map is a *statement* — someone's promise that the road goes on.'

identify:1.en: Bell held up a small glowing stone and turned it slowly in the starlight. 'We need to *identify* which island this came from,' she said, comparing it against hand-drawn charts spread across the deck. The stone hummed when she held it near the eastern edge of the map. We had our answer.
identify:1.cnHint: 小铃仔细研究发光石头，试图____它来自哪座岛屿。
identify:1.hook: The stone's hum grew louder as the eastern clouds began to part.
identify:1.line: 'Help me *identify* this marking — I've never seen it on any chart before.'

comprehension:1.en: Old Helm handed me a page of symbols from the word-bank and watched me work through them. My *comprehension* was slow at first, each symbol a small puzzle, but by the third line I felt something click and the meaning opened up like a door. He smiled without saying a word.
comprehension:1.cnHint: 我慢慢读懂了符号页，____能力在练习中逐渐提升。
comprehension:1.hook: The last symbol on the page was one Old Helm himself had never solved.
comprehension:1.line: 'Your *comprehension* is growing fast — you read that in half the time I expected.'

require:1.en: Crossing to the next island would *require* three things, Old Helm explained: a spoken word, a steady hand on the rope, and the courage not to look down. I had managed two of the three before. He did not say which one I was still missing, but his look told me everything.
require:1.cnHint: 老舵手解释说，跨越到下一座岛____三个条件才能成功。
require:1.hook: I already knew which of the three I was still missing.
require:1.line: 'The crossing will *require* every bit of focus you have — do not waste it.'

least:1.en: Of all the islands we had visited, this one was the *least* decorated — no banners, no carved stones, just open grass and a single wooden post at its centre. But Bell said the quiet ones always hid the best words. She was right. The post had six new fragments nailed to it.
least:1.cnHint: 这座岛是我们见过装饰____的一座，却藏着最好的线索。
least:1.hook: Six fragments, but the post had slots for seven.
least:1.line: 'At *least* look at the post before you decide there is nothing here.'

following:1.en: We launched from the island just before dawn, and the *following* wind caught our sails so perfectly that Bell laughed out loud. 'The sky wants us to move,' she said. The next island appeared on the horizon within minutes, its lights blinking like a quiet invitation.
following:1.cnHint: 出发后顺风相送，____的风让帆船轻松飞驰向新的目的地。
following:1.hook: The island's lights blinked twice — then one of them went dark.
following:1.line: 'With a *following* wind like this, we will reach the next island before sunrise.'

decide:1.en: The two paths split right at the centre of the island. One led toward a forest thick with silver leaves; the other dropped toward a lower platform where old barrels sat in rows. Old Helm looked at me. 'You *decide*,' he said simply. It was the first time he had ever said that. I chose the forest.
decide:1.cnHint: 两条路摆在面前，老舵手让我来____走哪一条。
decide:1.hook: From the forest, something answered back — soft, clear, and not quite human.
decide:1.line: 'It is your turn to *decide* — the troupe will follow wherever you lead.'

least:0.en: Old Helm spread the map across the table. Every island had a name, a colour, a shape. 'We start with the *least* dangerous path,' he said, tapping a pale blue dot near the edge. I leaned in close. Even that small dot felt like the whole world waiting to open.
least:0.cnHint: 老舵主在桌上铺开地图，指着边缘最____危险的路线准备出发。
least:0.hook: But the pale blue dot was already beginning to glow.
least:0.line: 'We take the *least* risky road first, and still find wonders.'
